Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. - gitnexus-cli: Use when the user needs to run GitNexus CLI commands like analyze/index a repo, check status, clean the index, generate a wiki, or list indexed repos. Examples: "Index this repo", "Reanalyze the codebase", "Generate a wiki"
- gitnexus-debugging: Use when the user is debugging a bug, tracing an error, or asking why something fails. Examples: "Why is X failing?", "Where does this error come from?", "Trace this bug"
- gitnexus-exploring: Use when the user asks how code works, wants to understand architecture, trace execution flows, or explore unfamiliar parts of the codebase. Examples: "How does X work?", "What calls this function?", "Show me the auth flow"
- gitnexus-guide: Use when the user asks about GitNexus itself — available tools, how to query the knowledge graph, MCP resources, graph schema, or workflow reference. Examples: "What GitNexus tools are available?", "How do I use GitNexus?"
- gitnexus-impact-analysis: Use when the user wants to know what will break if they change something, or needs safety analysis before editing code. Examples: "Is it safe to change X?", "What depends on this?", "What will break?"
- gitnexus-pdg-query: Use when querying or extending GitNexus's PDG control/data-dependence surface (the `pdg_query` MCP tool, CDG/REACHING_DEF edges), or reasoning about "what controls X" / "where does Y flow" / guard clauses. Examples: "what guards this statement?", "trace this variable within the function", "why is the pdg_query result empty?", "add a CDG query".
- gitnexus-pr-review: Use when the user wants to review a pull request, understand what a PR changes, assess risk of merging, or check for missing test coverage. Examples: "Review this PR", "What does PR #42 change?", "Is this PR safe to merge?"
- gitnexus-refactoring: Use when the user wants to rename, extract, split, move, or restructure code safely. Examples: "Rename this function", "Extract this into a module", "Refactor this class", "Move this to a separate file"
- gitnexus-taint-analysis: Use when working on, reviewing, or extending GitNexus's CFG/taint/PDG subsystem (the `--pdg` layers), or when reasoning about source→sink data-flow findings. Examples: "How does taint analysis work here?", "Why didn't explain find this flow?", "Add a new sink/source", "Review the interprocedural taint code".
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.

15	func (s *APIV1Service) ListMemoReactions(ctx context.Context, request *v1pb.ListMemoReactionsRequest) (*v1pb.ListMemoReactionsResponse, error) {
16		// Extract memo UID and check visibility.
17		memoUID, err := ExtractMemoUIDFromName(request.Name)
18		if err != nil {
19			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "invalid memo name: %v", err)
20		}
21		memo, err := s.Store.GetMemo(ctx, &store.FindMemo{UID: &memoUID})
22		if err != nil {
23			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get memo: %v", err)
24		}
25		if memo == nil {
26			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.NotFound, "memo not found")
27		}
28	
29		// Check memo visibility.
30		if memo.Visibility != store.Public {
31			user, err := s.fetchCurrentUser(ctx)
32			if err != nil {
33				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get user")
34			}
35			if user == nil {
36				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Unauthenticated, "user not authenticated")
37			}
38			if memo.Visibility == store.Private && memo.CreatorID != user.ID && !isSuperUser(user) {
39				return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "permission denied")
40			}
41		}
42	
43		reactions, err := s.Store.ListReactions(ctx, &store.FindReaction{
44			ContentID: &request.Name,
45		})
46		if err != nil {
47			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to list reactions")
48		}
49	
50		response := &v1pb.ListMemoReactionsResponse{
51			Reactions: []*v1pb.Reaction{},
52		}
53		response.Reactions, err = s.convertReactionsFromStoreWithCreators(ctx, reactions, nil)
54		if err != nil {
55			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to convert reactions")
56		}
57		return response, nil
58	}

60	func (s *APIV1Service) UpsertMemoReaction(ctx context.Context, request *v1pb.UpsertMemoReactionRequest) (*v1pb.Reaction, error) {
61		user, err := s.fetchCurrentUser(ctx)
62		if err != nil {
63			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get current user")
64		}
65		if user == nil {
66			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Unauthenticated, "user not authenticated")
67		}
68	
69		// Extract memo UID and check visibility before allowing reaction.
70		memoUID, err := ExtractMemoUIDFromName(request.Reaction.ContentId)
71		if err != nil {
72			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "invalid memo name: %v", err)
73		}
74		memo, err := s.Store.GetMemo(ctx, &store.FindMemo{UID: &memoUID})
75		if err != nil {
76			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get memo: %v", err)
77		}
78		if memo == nil {
79			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.NotFound, "memo not found")
80		}
81	
82		// Check memo visibility.
83		if memo.Visibility == store.Private && memo.CreatorID != user.ID && !isSuperUser(user) {
84			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "permission denied")
85		}
86	
87		reaction, err := s.Store.UpsertReaction(ctx, &store.Reaction{
88			CreatorID:    user.ID,
89			ContentID:    request.Reaction.ContentId,
90			ReactionType: request.Reaction.ReactionType,
91		})
92		if err != nil {
93			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to upsert reaction")
94		}
95	
96		reactionMessage, err := s.convertReactionFromStore(ctx, reaction)
97		if err != nil {
98			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to convert reaction")
99		}
100	
101		// Broadcast live refresh event (reaction belongs to a memo).
102		var parentMemo *store.Memo
103		if memo.ParentUID != nil {
104			parentMemo, _ = s.Store.GetMemo(ctx, &store.FindMemo{UID: memo.ParentUID})
105		}
106		s.SSEHub.Broadcast(buildMemoReactionSSEEvent(SSEEventReactionUpserted, request.Reaction.ContentId, memo, parentMemo))
107	
108		return reactionMessage, nil
109	}

111	func (s *APIV1Service) DeleteMemoReaction(ctx context.Context, request *v1pb.DeleteMemoReactionRequest) (*emptypb.Empty, error) {
112		user, err := s.fetchCurrentUser(ctx)
113		if err != nil {
114			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get current user: %v", err)
115		}
116		if user == nil {
117			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Unauthenticated, "user not authenticated")
118		}
119	
120		_, reactionID, err := ExtractMemoReactionIDFromName(request.Name)
121		if err != nil {
122			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "invalid reaction name: %v", err)
123		}
124	
125		// Get reaction and check ownership.
126		reaction, err := s.Store.GetReaction(ctx, &store.FindReaction{
127			ID: &reactionID,
128		})
129		if err != nil {
130			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get reaction")
131		}
132		if reaction == nil {
133			// Return permission denied to avoid revealing if reaction exists.
134			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "permission denied")
135		}
136	
137		if reaction.CreatorID != user.ID && !isSuperUser(user) {
138			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "permission denied")
139		}
140	
141		if err := s.Store.DeleteReaction(ctx, &store.DeleteReaction{
142			ID: reactionID,
143		}); err != nil {
144			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to delete reaction")
145		}
146	
147		memoUID, err := ExtractMemoUIDFromName(reaction.ContentID)
148		if err != nil {
149			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.InvalidArgument, "invalid memo name: %v", err)
150		}
151		memo, err := s.Store.GetMemo(ctx, &store.FindMemo{UID: &memoUID})
152		if err != nil {
153			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get memo")
154		}
155	
156		// Broadcast live refresh event (reaction belongs to a memo).
157		var parentMemo *store.Memo
158		if memo != nil && memo.ParentUID != nil {
159			parentMemo, _ = s.Store.GetMemo(ctx, &store.FindMemo{UID: memo.ParentUID})
160		}
161		s.SSEHub.Broadcast(buildMemoReactionSSEEvent(SSEEventReactionDeleted, reaction.ContentID, memo, parentMemo))
162	
163		return &emptypb.Empty{}, nil
164	}
